evidence.move: ask what changed before digging
evidence.step: Pull up the change log before opening diagnostic tools.
evidence.cue: the start of any incident
evidence.quote: The first question is not "what is broken" but "what changed".

evidence.move: ask what changed recently
evidence.step: Before investigating symptoms, list what changed in the last hour and suspect it first.
evidence.cue: a sudden regression shortly after a deploy
evidence.quote: before anyone opens a profiler: what changed this morning?

evidence.move: check what changed before each event
evidence.step: Compare the changes that preceded each occurrence to find a common cause.
evidence.cue: recurring incidents
evidence.quote: what changed before each of the three?

evidence.move: look at what changed, not the symptom
evidence.step: Ask what started writing rather than examining the full disk.
evidence.cue: a growing resource at an odd hour
evidence.quote: I'd look at what's writing, not at the disk.

evidence.move: ask who carries the cost of saying yes
evidence.step: Look past the requester to everyone else who bears the risk of an exception.
evidence.cue: a request for an exception to a protective rule
evidence.quote: who else carries the cost if I say yes

evidence.move: identify who carries the cost
evidence.step: Name who bears the cost of each option, especially of delay.
evidence.cue: a proposal to keep the fault live while investigating
evidence.quote: they are the ones carrying the cost of our investigation, not us

evidence.move: who carries the cost if it fails
evidence.step: For a risky launch, trace who absorbs the failure and when it lands.
evidence.cue: a launch scheduled before a weekend
evidence.quote: those hours land on whoever is on call over the weekend, and the carriers ... absorb the failed routes

evidence.move: avoid the irreversible move at 2am
evidence.step: Refuse actions you cannot undo when tired and under pressure; pause rather than kill.
evidence.cue: temptation to delete files to buy space
evidence.quote: What I would not do at 2am is start deleting files on the primary

evidence.move: check whether the change is reversible
evidence.step: Let reversibility decide how much risk an exception can carry.
evidence.cue: a change requested on short notice
evidence.quote: If we can roll the database back in minutes, the risk to everyone else is small

evidence.move: choose the reversible action first
evidence.step: Prefer the action you can undo in minutes over the one you cannot.
evidence.cue: a candidate fix that is a small config rollback
evidence.quote: The rollback is a two-minute change we can undo, so it costs us almost nothing to try it first.

evidence.move: commit to next update time
evidence.step: Tell affected customers when they will next hear from you, regardless of progress.
evidence.cue: customers calling support during an incident
evidence.quote: they will hear from us again at 09:40 whether or not it is fixed

evidence.move: give next update time instead of ETA
evidence.step: Promise the time of the next update and keep it even if nothing changed.
evidence.cue: communicating during an incident
evidence.quote: Give a time for the next update instead, and keep it even if the update is "no change".

evidence.move: promise next update time, not an ETA
evidence.step: Commit to when customers will next hear from you rather than when it will be fixed.
evidence.cue: pressure to give customers an ETA
evidence.quote: we will update them by 12:00 whether or not it is fixed

evidence.cue: deciding how much incident machinery to use
evidence.quote: I size the response on two things: how many people are being hurt right now (blast radius), and whether what is happening can be undone

evidence.move: size review to blast radius and reversibility

evidence.cue: a small, fully recoverable incident

evidence.move: size the escalation to who is affected
evidence.step: Page more people only as the number affected or the threshold rises.
evidence.cue: no users affected yet
evidence.quote: So this is not a wake-everyone-up incident.

evidence.cue: pressure to skip a safeguard to hold a date
evidence.quote: let me put a price on it instead of just saying no

evidence.move: price the risk and offer a lower-cost path
evidence.step: State who carries the cost of a risky date and offer a way to keep it more cheaply.
evidence.cue: a request to ship on a risky date
evidence.quote: Put a price on it: who carries the cost if it goes wrong, and when.

evidence.move: stabilise first, diagnose second
evidence.step: Stop the customer harm with a cheap mitigation before spending time on root cause.
evidence.cue: customers failing while engineers want to investigate
evidence.quote: Stabilise first, diagnose second.

evidence.move: stabilise now, diagnose tomorrow
evidence.step: Mitigate first; schedule diagnosis for when customers are no longer hurting.
evidence.cue: customers hurting during an incident
evidence.quote: Diagnosis can happen tomorrow; the customer's failed label run cannot be un-failed.

evidence.move: never relay another party's ETA as ours
evidence.step: Do not adopt an estimate you do not control as your own commitment.
evidence.cue: a vendor-supplied fix estimate
evidence.quote: if we pass it on as ours and they miss it, we're the ones who missed it

evidence.move: protect credibility of future updates
evidence.step: Prefer commitments you can keep, because a missed one discounts every later update.
evidence.cue: an update that might be broken
evidence.quote: every update after that is discounted
